title: Choose Digest’s visual world
question: A calm reading experience is fixed by the brief. Choose the form it should take across the landing page, service settings, and digest reader.

options.label: The Daily Letter
options.lineage: personal correspondence and dated letter sheets
options.thesis: Your feeds become one quiet letter worth opening.
options.viewport: The first screen shows a legible example letter, its section index, and a clear invitation to start.
options.risk: The correspondence metaphor could become decoration if the reader is not truly faster to scan.

raised.raise: The example digest owns the first viewport as one decisive object.
Active sections and connected services have unmistakable persistent states.
Progress unfolds in one readable sequence rather than scattered motion.
Dense information aligns to a precise scanning grid without visual strobing.
One restrained accent marks only actions and incomplete results.

options.label: The Reading Brief
options.thesis: A daily briefing replaces three infinite feeds with a finite read.
options.viewport: A full-scale example brief leads, with a contents rail and a single Start action.
options.risk: This is the familiar editorial route many digest products could choose.

options.label: The Memory Quilt
options.thesis: A personal network becomes an atlas of dated human moments.
options.viewport: An unequal patch grid holds example posts, each with its source and date sewn to the edge.
options.case: Personal stories identify well with the audience, though the patchwork slows text scanning.
options.risk: The varied blocks can reproduce the visual competition the product is trying to escape.

options.label: The Flash Sleeve
options.thesis: Posts are marked directly onto a photographic surface.
options.viewport: A photographed feed scene fills the screen with marked entries.
options.case: It identifies with feed culture but contradicts the promised quiet reading.
options.kept: A decisive single focal object in the first viewport.

options.label: The Football Kit
options.lineage: team crests, numbers, and sleeve patches
options.thesis: Connected services become teams on a kit wall.
options.viewport: A numbered kit organizes active services and the current digest.
options.case: Team identity is unrelated to the personal reading task.
options.risk: Large numerals displace the digest itself.
options.kept: Persistent active states across navigation and service settings.

options.label: The Film Strip
options.thesis: The feed is edited into a short sequence of readable frames.
options.viewport: A sequence of selected moments moves across a perforated strip.
options.case: Editing conveys selection, but media framing dominates the text.

options.label: The Barcode Field
options.viewport: An indexed data field fills the page behind selected entries.
options.case: Its precision aids scanning, but strobing contradicts the product promise.
options.risk: The form is harsher than the feeds it replaces.
options.kept: A rigorous alignment grid for dense information.

options.label: The Meter Bridge
options.thesis: A visual signal bridge shows which services yielded useful activity.
options.viewport: Needles show filtered signal, with the readable digest below.
options.case: The signal idea is apt, but meters delay access to the text.
options.risk: A decorative instrument could become the new distraction.
options.kept: A restricted accent for thresholds, actions, and incomplete results.

canonCard.label: The familiar app layout
canonCard.thesis: A polished landing page and conventional product dashboard.
canonCard.viewport: A standard promise-and-action hero leads to a cards-based digest dashboard.
canonCard.risk: The form would be easy to confuse with other feed tools.
